items.title: Cross-thread submission-observation carve-outs
items.isolation_authority: #466 finding (CI-caught regression, reproduced under CPU pinning) + the #459 boundary clause (no oracle re-shaping inside M)
items.reason: Two sub-oracles submit from a helper thread and observe that submission's readiness from the host loop. That visibility is a compat-carrier property: the caller-owned cell is bound inside the submitting call, so the observing thread can see readiness, and the acceptance wake can be consumed, before the submitter hands anything back. The adopted responsibility travels with the returned Request, so the same loop shape can lose the wake and park to its watchdog. Retrying the migration at these two sites would mean re-shaping a §24 acceptance-shape oracle (an application-level handoff wait), which a test-only migration slice must not do silently.
items.surviving_behavior: Both host-loop oracles keep their mutant kills (obligation discovery, bounded wakes, quiescence at an idle fd) and pass under CPU pinning and on the CI runner; every other consumer in the same file runs on the adopted Request face.
items.exact_scope: tests/threadpool_external_loop_test.cpp: external_poll_loop_threadpool_w03 (`late`, submitted by the helper thread) and host_acknowledgement_racing_new_signal_never_strands (`racing`, submitted by the signaler thread), plus the compat helper submit_zero_op_into and the restored completion.hpp include
items.downstream_gating_effect: F2's carrier retirement must either publish an adopted cross-thread observation spelling or re-shape these two oracles explicitly and re-prove the acceptance shape; no M claim treats them as migrated.
items.exit_condition: F2 carrier retirement with the two oracles re-derived over an adopted handoff spelling (or explicitly re-shaped, with the §24 acceptance-shape claim re-proved).
evidence: pinned stress before the carve-out: the migrated spelling hard-aborted on the pinned host (one batch 25/25, retry 5/5) and produced the clean FAIL host_acknowledgement_racing_new_signal_never_strands under gdb; at unrestricted CPU counts the rate was lower (2-3 failures / 25 runs)
